title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Integration, Escalation, Health Checks, and QBR Template
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook describes the standard process, runbooks, and templates the Customer Success (CS) and Support teams use for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It covers: integration guidance, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, ongoing health checks, and a quarterly business review (QBR) template. The goal is a predictable, measurable onboarding experience that leads to an SLA-backed go-live and healthy long-term operation.

Scope:
- New enterprise customers adopting Redwood (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Integrations that include API usage, VPC/private network peering, and Dedicated capacity.
- Handover from Solutions Engineering to Customer Success and Support.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Technical Account Managers (TAMs)
- Support engineers and on-call SREs
- Solutions Engineers and Integrators

Key goals / success metrics:
- Time-to-first-successful-inference (from account creation): target < 7 days
- End-to-end integration completion (all routes validated): target < 21 days
- First 30-day retention: customer issuing >= 10k tokens or equivalent workload within 30 days
- Escalation SLA: initial triage response within 4 hours business hours; P1 MTTR target 2 hours

Roles and ownership:
- Customer Success (owner): onboarding coordination, customer-facing communications, QBRs
- Solutions Engineering (owner): pre-onboard architecture review, integration support
- Support (owner): 24x7 incident triage, bug tracking, workarounds
- Eng-SRE (owner): escalation for platform or infra incidents, capacity requests
- Product (owner): feature requests and model/behavior regressions

Onboarding phases (high level)

1) Pre-onboard (Discovery & Planning)
- Deliverables: integration plan, security requirements, SLA expectations, project kickoff agenda
- Steps:
  1. Kickoff meeting (CSM, SE, customer PM, security lead) — confirm timelines and success criteria.
  2. Collect security & network requirements (IP allowlist, VPC design, compliance needs).
  3. Identify models and expected traffic profile (tokens/sec, avg seq length, concurrency).
  4. Assign owners and schedule weekly checkpoints.

2) Integration (Network, Auth, and API)
- Deliverables: validated network connectivity, working API calls, example prompts, and model pinning config
- Steps:
  1. Provide API keys and least-privilege credentials via secure channel.
  2. Network connectivity options (choose one):
     - Hosted: public API with customer IP allowlist and mTLS if requested
     - Dedicated: private peering (VPC/VPN) + reserved capacity config
     - Private: on-prem appliance or VPC deployment checklist
  3. Docs and sample curl/SDK requests (include streaming and function-calling examples).
  4. Validate basic end-to-end inference using a canonical prompt from the customer.
  5. Configure model pinning and rollout policy for initial production (canary percent, fallback model).

Sample networking & security checklist (to include in customer ticket):
- Required TLS: 1.2+ (prefer TLS 1.3)
- API endpoints: https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/inference (replace with tenant-specific URL for Dedicated/Private)
- IP/CIDR allowlist: request customer's list; provide instructions for dynamic egress via cloud provider when needed
- VPC peering: confirm route table propagation and security groups for outbound 443
- KMS/HSM: provide integration guide if customer requires BYOK

3) Validation (Functional, Perf, Security)
- Deliverables: test plan results, performance baselines, security sign-off
- Steps:
  1. Execute functional test plan: correctness, hallucination checks, retries and idempotency tests.
  2. Run performance tests: baseline latency P50/P95, throughput tests at expected concurrency, and prefix/KV cache warmup checks. Record results in the onboarding ticket.
  3. Security validation: encryption at rest, access control, audit logging verification.
  4. Confirm billing and quota limits for initial production traffic.

4) Go-live & Handoff
- Criteria for go-live:
  - All functional tests pass with acceptance criteria
  - Performance baseline within expected SLOs (P95 latency below agreed threshold)
  - Security checklist completed and signed off
  - Billing and quotas provisioned
- Handoff:
  - SE hands off technical ownership to TAM and Support with a handover doc and runbook
  - CSM schedules 1/7/30 day check-ins post go-live

5) Post-go-live / Optimization
- Use Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching/quantization profiles and cache config
- Track unit economics: cost/token, latency impact, and error rates
- Escalation readiness: ensure runbooks present and on-call rotation known to customer

Integration guide: specific configurations and examples

Authentication and API examples (canonical)
- Use SDK or curl with API key header: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>
- Sample curl (replace host with tenant endpoint):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-1.0", "prompt":"Summarize the following...", "max_tokens":256}'

Model pinning and rollout example (JSON snippet for customer config):
- model: rwd-llm-1.0
- fallback_model: rwd-llm-1.0-quantized
- canary_percentage: 10
- timeout_ms: 30000

Escalation playbook (triage & handoffs)

Severity definitions and routing:
- P1 (Platform down / customer-facing outage): critical user operations failing, multiple customers impacted or single enterprise with major outage.
  - Initial triage: Support 15 minutes, page on-call eng-sre.
  - Communication cadence: initial update 30 minutes, then every 60 minutes until resolved.
  - Target MTTR: 2 hours (engineer-led), record incident in incident tracker and run postmortem.
- P2 (Degraded performance / data correctness): significant impairment for a customer without full outage.
  - Initial triage: Support 1 hour.
  - Target MTTR: 24 hours for rollback/workaround, 72 hours for permanent fix if code change required.
- P3 (Minor bug / feature request): low-impact bugs or documentation issues.
  - Initial triage: Support during next business hours.
  - Target resolution: next release or scheduled fix depending on priority.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Support creates ticket with reproducible steps, logs, sample requests, and correlation IDs.
2. If required, Support pages Eng-SRE with priority tag and attaches telemetry (traces, logs, SLO alerts).
3. Eng-SRE identifies mitigation (capacity increase, rollback, config change) and implements temporary controls.
4. Product/Runtime team notified for root cause and permanent fix.
5. Postmortem and RCA published within 5 business days for P1 incidents.

Communications templates (use ticket system macros)
- Initial acknowledgement (to customer):
  "Thanks — we've received your report (ticket #{ticket}). Our on-call engineer is investigating and we will update within 30 minutes."
- Status update (to internal stakeholders):
  "P1 active — initial triage complete. Current hypothesis: <short-hypothesis>. Actions taken: <list>. Next update: <time>. Owner: <engineer>."

Known issues & workarounds (living list)

| Issue | Impact | Workaround | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Cold KV cache causing high first-request latency for long contexts (> 8k tokens) | Elevated P95 on first request (~2–6s extra) | Warm cache with a short batch of representative requests or pre-warm via synthetic prefix requests during deployment | eng-serving-runtime |
| High variance in P95 latency under bursty concurrency on specific GPU types | Intermittent slower responses for medium concurrency (50–200 concurrent) | Route bursty traffic to Dedicated or increase burst capacity; use smaller batch windows for latency-sensitive routes | eng-sre / capacity-planning |
| Function-calling structured outputs sometimes truncated when using streaming + large functions | Corrupted JSON output in client implementations | Recommend non-streamed calls for critical structured outputs or increase chunk buffer and validate final chunk assembly client-side | eng-developer-experience |
| Tokenization differences vs. upstream: tiny token-count mismatches causing billing delta | Observed small token counts differences compared to customer tokenizer | Share canonical tokenizer and advise customers to use Redwood tokenizer for billing alignment; open ticket for tokenization parity if needed | applied-ml-and-evals |

(If you identify a persistent issue not on this list, add it to the ticket and tag the appropriate owner. This table is reviewed monthly by Support leads.)

Health checks, dashboards, and SLOs

Standard SLOs we report to enterprise customers:
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for Hosted API (subject to contract)
- Latency: P95 <= agreed threshold (example 500 ms for low-latency tier)
- Error rate: <= 0.5% 4xx/5xx for stable routes
- Data durability: Audit logs and request traces retained per contract (e.g., 90 days or customer-specific retention)

Suggested dashboards (Redwood Console pre-built views):
- Per-tenant latency (P50/P95/P99) and request volume by route/model
- Error budget burn (daily and 30-day) and top error types
- Cost by route (token-level cost breakdown) and top spenders
- Model quality regression dashboards (prompt-set based evals over time)

Daily/weekly health checklist (to be completed by CSM/TAM during early weeks)
- Daily (first 14 days): check 24-hour error rate, latency anomalies, and quota usage
- Weekly (first 8 weeks): validate growth against forecast, check for model regressions, review any open P2/P1 tickets
- Monthly: billing reconciliation and post-launch optimization review

QBR template (quarterly deliverable)

Agenda (60 minutes):
1. Executive summary (5 min): adoption highlights, health, and risks
2. Usage and economics (10 min): tokens, cost per token, route-level spend, forecast vs actual
3. Performance and reliability (10 min): SLO adherence, incidents since last QBR, mitigation status
4. Product & roadmap (10 min): relevant new features, model catalog changes, upcoming deprecations
5. Optimization opportunities (10 min): batching/quantization suggestions, model changes to reduce cost or improve latency
6. Action items & owners (10 min): prioritized list and next steps

Pre-read materials (to send 3 days before QBR):
- Last quarter's usage CSV, incident summary, and current model pinning config

QBR deliverables (post-meeting)
- Action item tracker with owners and ETA
- Updated optimization recommendations and projected unit-economics impact
- Follow-up technical deep-dive if required (scheduled within 2 weeks)

Templates and checklists attached (copy/paste ready)

- Kickoff agenda checklist:
  - Intro & success metrics confirmed
  - Security contacts & certs provided
  - Initial test plan signed off

- Onboarding runbook (short form):
  1. Confirm API key distribution and network config
  2. Validate sanity request and record trace IDs
  3. Execute perf baseline run and upload results
  4. Run security checklist and obtain sign-off
  5. Schedule go-live and update stakeholders

Contacts and escalation matrix
